title: GraphFI: An Efficient Fault Injection Framework for Graph Processing on GPGPUs
problem: Existing fault injection methods ignore graph-specific execution paradigms (iterations, vertices, error propagation), producing inaccurate system error resilience characterization and blind fault injection trials that are computationally expensive.
method: GraphFI exploits three graph-specific properties: iteration-driven FI (selecting representative iterations with similar active vertex sets), topology-driven FI (identifying resilience-similarity communities and testing representative vertices), and monotonicity-driven FI (using fault monotonic properties to predict severe error boundaries). Merging all three approaches reduces fault site space by up to 100x.

title: 33.4: A Wideband Bidirectional Calibration-Free Frequency/Switching-Staggering 360° D-Band Phase Shifter with Frequency-Invariant Codes Achieving lt; 2.38°/0.63dB RMS-Errors Over 24% Bandwidth
problem: D-band (110-170GHz) phased arrays for 6G require compact, bidirectional phase shifters (PSs) with 360° range, fine resolution (~4-6b), low phase/gain error, frequency-independent codes, and low power—existing designs trade off area, accuracy, or bandwidth.
method: A wideband D-band phase shifter uses frequency/switching-staggering technique to achieve frequency-invariant phase codes across 24% bandwidth. Bidirectional architecture enables TX/RX sharing. Calibration-free design with <2.38° RMS phase error and <0.63dB RMS gain error eliminates runtime tuning.

title: Late Breaking Results: Encoder-Decoder Generative Diffusion Transformer Towards Push-Button Analog IC Sizing
problem: Analog IC sizing relies on time-consuming optimization-based methods that lack scalability and generalization to unseen performance targets.
method: Encoder-decoder diffusion transformer (attention-based generative model) solves inverse analog sizing problem by sampling accurate solutions at push-button speed, trained on performance targets to generalize beyond training set.

title: CROSS: Compiler-Driven Optimization of Sparse DNNs Using Sparse/Dense Computation Kernels
problem: Exploiting DNN weight sparsity on GPUs is hindered by the overhead of index-based encoding/decoding required by sparse formats, making sparse computation kernels slower than dense kernels even at high sparsity ratios.
method: CROSS is an end-to-end compilation framework that analyzes parameter distribution locality to identify regions where dense computation remains efficient. It decomposes sparse DNN workloads into multiple components across different sparsity levels and maps each component to either a specialized sparse kernel or a high-performance dense kernel. A novel sparse graph translation technique transforms the sparse computation graph into a form compatible with dense computation kernels, reconciling the sparse DNN computation with optimized BLAS-level dense routines on GPU. The framework accommodates various sparsity patterns (unstructured, structured, N:M) and optimization techniques.

title: LightRIM: Light Runtime Integrity Measurement for Linux Kernels in Embedded Applications
problem: Linux kernel security modules provide integrity monitoring but consume substantial computational resources, making them unsuitable for resource-limited embedded systems like autonomous vehicles and robots.
method: LightRIM performs two-stage hashing on monitored kernel objects and uses event-triggered measurement tied to security value changes. A heuristic algorithm maximizes attack detection rate within CPU budget constraints via randomized measurement intervals to mitigate TOCTOU vulnerabilities.

title: Earth+: On-Board Satellite Imagery Compression Leveraging Historical Earth Observations
problem: Satellite downlink capacity is so limited that over 90% of captured earth-observation images are never downloaded; existing on-board compression techniques treat each image independently and cannot exploit the rich temporal and spatial redundancy available across an entire satellite constellation.
method: Earth+ implements a change-detection-based compression pipeline on the satellite. Ground stations upload recently captured reference images from other satellites in the same constellation to each on-board satellite via the uplink. On-board processing compares each newly captured image against the latest matching reference image and transmits only the changed regions (delta encoding). The system manages reference image currency and on-board storage to ensure that references are temporally close to the captured images, maximizing delta sparsity and thus compression.

title: BrokenSleep: Remote Power Timing Attack Exploiting Processor Idle States
problem: Modern processors support multiple C-state (idle) levels with different wake-up latencies; an attacker can remotely detect which C-state a victim processor core is in by measuring network response timing, enabling covert and side-channel communication across nodes without requiring co-location on the same machine.
method: BrokenSleep exploits the deterministic wake-up latency differences between processor C-states (C0 active, C1/C1E/C6 sleep) to encode information in the timing of network responses from a victim server. The attacker sends network requests and measures response latency; the victim's current C-state (determined by its workload idle pattern) is deduced from the latency profile. Both covert channel (data exfiltration across security boundaries without direct network access) and side-channel (keystroke timing inference) variants are demonstrated. The attack affects both Intel and ARM processors, exploiting standard ACPI power management without any microarchitectural vulnerability.

title: On Design Space Exploration of Cache System in Multi-Chiplet Systems
problem: Multi-chiplet systems have complex cache hierarchies spanning multiple dies with varying topologies; existing design space exploration methods (NN-Baton, IntLP) fail to optimize cache subsystem performance or explore the full design space efficiently.
method: Proposes bilevel optimization algorithm that models cache miss rates and network latency as functions of hierarchy and interconnect parameters; iteratively solves two subproblems: (1) cache subsystem optimization and (2) inter-chiplet interconnection network optimization to minimize concurrent average memory access time (C-AMAT) under cost/power constraints.

title: CirSTAG: Circuit Stability Analysis on Graph-based Manifolds
problem: Circuit stability (sensitivity) analysis requires numerous time-consuming simulations to estimate how parameter variations (gate sizes, capacitance) impact circuit performance. Existing methods struggle with scalability for large integrated circuits.
method: CirSTAG uses graph neural networks to analyze circuit stability through a spectral framework examining input/output graph manifolds. The method calculates a stability score equivalent to the local Lipschitz constant for each node and edge, considering both graph structure and node feature perturbations. When adjacent nodes on the input manifold map to remote nodes on the output manifold (mapping distortion), this indicates poor GNN stability and identifies critical circuit elements.

title: SimPhony: A Device-Circuit-Architecture Cross-Layer Modeling and Simulation Framework for Heterogeneous Electronic-Photonic AI System
problem: Electronic-photonic integrated circuits (EPICs) for AI require innovations across devices, circuits, architecture, and design automation. Lack of unified simulation framework prevents exploration of hardware innovations and evaluation on common benchmarks.
method: SimPhony provides cross-layer modeling and simulation: generic extensible hardware topology for heterogeneous multi-core photonic tensor cores; optics-specific dataflow with multi-dimensional parallelism; data-aware energy modeling with device responses, area estimation, link budget and bandwidth-adaptive memory; seamless hardware/software co-simulation integration with model training frameworks.

title: WarpDrive: GPU-Based Fully Homomorphic Encryption Acceleration Leveraging Tensor and CUDA Cores
problem: GPU-based acceleration of Fully Homomorphic Encryption (FHE) is bottlenecked by frequent pipeline stalls from memory-latency-bound Number Theoretic Transform (NTT) operations and by suboptimal utilization of GPU hardware units, leaving both CUDA Cores and Tensor Cores underused for FHE workloads.
method: WarpDrive applies three key optimizations: (1) computation decomposition of NTT that reduces total instruction count by 73% through arithmetic restructuring; (2) fine-grained memory access design that pipelines loads to eliminate 86% of pipeline stalls; (3) a concurrent-execution framework that runs CUDA Cores and Tensor Cores simultaneously within a single NTT kernel — the first such combined use — exploiting both unit types' complementary throughput characteristics. Additionally, intra-ciphertext parallelism is maximally extracted without requiring ciphertext batching.

title: GPS: GNN-Based Two-Stage Pre-Scheduling Loop Mapping Method on CGRAs
problem: Coarse-grained reconfigurable architecture (CGRA) compilers must generate effective loop mappings for complex applications within tight time budgets, but the large search space makes optimal mapping intractable.
method: GPS combines Integer Linear Programming (ILP) for initial mapping constraints with Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) for solution refinement. The two-stage approach significantly reduces the search space before full ILP optimization, accelerating the mapping process while improving quality. The GNN learns to identify promising mapping candidates and prune the search space.

title: ChipAlign: Instruction Alignment in Large Language Models for Chip Design via Geodesic Interpolation
problem: Chip-specific LLMs like ChipNeMo lack instruction alignment capability, limiting their ability to follow explicit human directives and serve as practical assistant chatbots for hardware design engineers.
method: ChipAlign uses geodesic interpolation in weight space to merge instruction-aligned and chip-specific LLMs without training, fusing weights along the manifold to produce a model that inherits both strong instruction following and chip domain knowledge.

title: GoPIM: GCN-Oriented Pipeline Optimization for PIM Accelerators
problem: ReRAM-based PIM accelerators for GCN training suffer from severe pipeline underutilization due to skewed execution times across GCN stages (aggregation, combination) and skewed degree distributions of graph vertices, causing crossbar resource imbalance.
method: GoPIM employs an ML-based scheme that dynamically allocates ReRAM crossbar resources to the most needed pipeline stages to streamline overall execution and eliminate stage bottlenecks. A selective vertex updating technique interleaves vertex mapping across crossbars to evenly distribute vertices despite skewed degree distributions. These two mechanisms reduce overall execution time while maintaining accuracy. A practical architecture design for GoPIM is also provided.

title: Mr.TPL: A Method for Multi-Pin Net Router in Triple Patterning Lithography
problem: Triple patterning lithography (TPL) requires layout decomposition into three masks; multi-pin routing creates excessive color conflicts and stitches, especially for nets with >2 terminals.
method: Mr.TPL extends TPL-aware routing to multi-pin nets via novel color assignment and stitch-reduction algorithms; optimizes routing topology to minimize conflicts across three mask layers.

title: SeDA: Secure and Efficient DNN Accelerators with Hardware/Software Synergy
problem: Securing DNN accelerators with encryption and integrity verification incurs significant hardware resource overhead and off-chip memory access penalties.
method: SeDA proposes: 1) bandwidth-aware encryption mechanism improving hardware efficiency, 2) optimal block granularity via intra/inter-layer tiling patterns, 3) multi-level integrity verification minimizing or eliminating memory access overheads.
